title: CivWorldBench: Evaluating Language World Models in Structured Multi-Agent Sandbox Worlds
abstract: arXiv:2610.16450v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The growing use of language models for forecasting motivates a broader evaluation of their world-model capabilities. Such evaluation must go beyond predictive accuracy to assess hidden-state inference and intervention prediction. Real-world forecasting benchmarks offer limited access to hidden-state ground truth and controlled experiments. We introduce CivWorldBench, a benchmark built on a multi-agent strategy game engine with recorded internal states, controlled observations, and paired intervention rollouts. Its 1,900 decision points from 475 worlds support three task levels: association forecasting, belief inference, and intervention prediction. Reference predictors support attributable evaluation of capability gaps, with an expert harness and empirical ceiling estimates contextualizing scores. translated_title: CivWorldBench：在结构化多智能体沙盒世界中评估语言世界模型
translated_abstract: 语言模型在预测任务中的日益广泛应用，促使人们需要对其世界模型能力进行更全面的评估。这种评估必须超越单纯的预测准确性，进而考察隐藏状态推断与干预预测能力。然而，现实世界的预测基准难以获取隐藏状态的真实标签，也无法开展受控实验。我们提出了CivWorldBench，该基准构建于多智能体策略游戏引擎之上，具备完整记录的内部状态、受控观测以及成对的干预推演。其来自475个世界的1,900个决策点支持三个任务层级：关联预测、信念推断和干预预测。参考预测器可支持对能力差距进行可归因的评估，并配有专家评估工具与经验上限估计来为分数提供参照背景。存储的轨迹使中间预测结果可被验证，而智能体对局实验则检验世界模型能力能否支持下游任务。
tldr: 该论文提出CivWorldBench基准，利用具备内部状态记录、受控观测和干预对照推演的多智能体策略游戏沙盒，从关联预测、信念推断和干预预测三个层级系统评估语言模型的世界建模能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CivWorldBench, a benchmark built on a multi-agent strategy game sandbox with recorded hidden states, controlled observations, and paired intervention rollouts, which evaluates language world models across three levels: association forecasting, belief inference, and intervention prediction.
